63960.e: The Quran is divided into chapters called surahs. Each surah is made up of verses.
63960.m: The chapters of the Quran are called surahs.

63962.q: Roughly how are the surahs in the Quran ordered?
a: Long ones first, short ones at the end
Short ones first, long ones at the end
63962.e: After the short first surah come the long surahs. Towards the end of the Quran the surahs get shorter and shorter.
63962.m: In the Quran the long surahs come first and the short ones at the end.

63963.q: Which language is also written with Arabic letters?
63963.e: Persian, the language spoken in Iran, is written with Arabic letters. A few extra letters are added.
63963.m: Persian is also written with Arabic letters.

63964.q: What is the raised pulpit in a mosque called?
63964.e: The minbar is a staircase with a platform. From there the imam gives the sermon at Friday prayers.
63964.m: The pulpit in a mosque is called the minbar.

63965.q: What does the Arabic word for mosque, “masjid”, mean?
63965.e: “Masjid” means a place where you prostrate yourself. When praying there, people touch the floor with their forehead.

63966.q: Where do women and men pray in many mosques?
63966.e: In many mosques women and men pray in separate areas. Sometimes women have their own room or a gallery.
63966.m: In many mosques women and men pray separately.

63967.q: What do children often learn at a mosque?
63967.e: Many mosques offer lessons for children. There they learn to read the Quran in Arabic and find out more about their religion.
63967.m: Children often learn to read the Quran at the mosque.

63968.q: What do people sit on in the prayer hall of a mosque?
63968.e: There are usually no benches in the prayer hall. The whole floor is covered with carpet, and people sit and pray on it.
63968.m: In a mosque you sit on the carpet.

63969.q: What do women usually wear when they visit a mosque?
63969.e: In the mosque women usually cover their hair with a scarf. Female visitors are often asked to do so too.
63969.m: Women usually wear a headscarf in a mosque.

63970.q: What do many mosques have for washing before prayer?
63970.e: Believers wash before prayer. That is why almost every mosque has a washroom or a fountain.
63970.m: Mosques have a washroom for the ritual washing.

63971.q: In which direction do Muslims lay their prayer mat to pray?
63971.e: Muslims pray facing the Kaaba in Mecca. So they lay the prayer mat so that it points there.
63971.m: The prayer mat points towards Mecca.

63972.q: When is the prayer called Isha said?
63972.e: The Isha prayer is the last of the five prayers. It is said when it has got dark.
63972.m: The Isha prayer is said at night.

63973.q: In Islamic tradition, what is whispered into a newborn baby's ear?
63973.e: By tradition, the call to prayer is whispered into the baby's right ear soon after birth. That way the first thing it hears is words about God.
63973.m: The call to prayer is whispered into a newborn baby's ear.

63974.q: At churches, what calls people to the service instead of a muezzin?
63974.e: Churches call believers by ringing their bells. At the mosque this job is done by the muezzin's call to prayer.
63974.m: At churches the bells call people to the service.

63975.q: What does the muezzin call on people to do in the call to prayer?
63975.e: In the call to prayer you hear the words “Come to prayer” and “Come to success”. This is how the muezzin invites the believers.
63975.m: The call to prayer says “Come to prayer”.

63976.q: How often in their life should a Muslim go on pilgrimage to Mecca if they are healthy and have enough money?
63976.e: The great pilgrimage to Mecca is one of the five pillars of Islam. Anyone who is healthy and can afford it should make it at least once in their life.
63976.m: You should go on pilgrimage to Mecca at least once in your life.

63977.q: On which mountain near Mecca do pilgrims pray on an important day of the pilgrimage?
63977.e: An important part of the pilgrimage is the day at Mount Arafat. There pilgrims pray from midday until sunset.
63977.m: Pilgrims pray for a whole day on Mount Arafat.

63978.q: What do pilgrims near Mecca throw at large stone walls?
63978.e: In Mina near Mecca, pilgrims throw small stones at three large walls that used to be pillars. This shows that they reject evil.
63978.m: Near Mecca pilgrims throw small stones at walls.

63979.q: When does the great pilgrimage to Mecca take place?
63979.e: The great pilgrimage takes place every year in the Islamic month of Dhu al-Hijjah. Because the Islamic calendar follows the moon, this month moves through the seasons.
63979.m: The great pilgrimage happens every year in a particular month.

63980.q: What is the landscape around Mecca like?
63980.e: Mecca lies in a dry valley between bare mountains. It rarely rains there.
63980.m: Mecca lies in a dry, mountainous area.

63981.q: What is the black cloth of the Kaaba embroidered with?
63981.e: The cloth over the Kaaba is called the kiswa. It is made of silk and embroidered with golden writing.
63981.m: The cloth of the Kaaba is embroidered with golden writing.

63982.q: Which way do Muslims face when they pray?
63982.e: Muslims pray facing the Kaaba in Mecca. In mosques a niche in the wall shows this direction.

63983.q: According to Islamic belief, who created the world?
63983.e: Muslims believe that God created heaven and earth and all life. That is why they thank him in prayer.
63983.m: According to Islamic belief, God created the world.

63984.q: Where do you start reading an Arabic book?
a: Where our last page would be
On the first page, as we do
In the middle of the book
At the bottom of each page
63984.e: Because Arabic is written from right to left, you open an Arabic book from the other side. The beginning is where our books end.
63984.m: An Arabic book starts where our last page would be.

63985.q: How many different forms can an Arabic letter have?
63985.e: A letter looks different depending on whether it stands alone or at the beginning, in the middle or at the end of a word. So it has up to four forms.
63985.m: An Arabic letter can have up to four forms.

63986.q: In which of these countries do people speak and write Arabic?
63986.e: Arabic is the official language in Egypt and in many other countries in North Africa and the Middle East.
63986.m: In Egypt people speak and write Arabic.

63987.q: Which English word comes from Arabic?
63987.e: The word sugar comes from the Arabic word “sukkar”. It reached English by way of other European languages.
63987.m: The word sugar comes from Arabic.

63988.q: What do you do with your mouth during the ritual washing?
63988.e: During the washing you take a little water into your mouth and rinse it out. Then you also clean your nose with water.
63988.m: During the washing you rinse your mouth with water.

63989.q: When is the prayer called Asr said?
63989.e: The Asr prayer is the third prayer of the day. It is said in the afternoon, when the shadows grow longer.
63989.m: The Asr prayer is said in the afternoon.

63990.q: What often hangs from the ceiling of large mosques?
63990.e: In many large mosques, splendid chandeliers with lots of lamps hang down. They light up the wide prayer hall.
63990.m: Splendid chandeliers often hang in large mosques.

63991.q: What is the shortest surah of the Quran called?
63991.e: The shortest surah is Al-Kawthar with only three verses. It comes near the end of the Quran.
63991.m: The shortest surah is called Al-Kawthar.

63992.q: What do many adult Muslims do during the day in the month of Ramadan?
63992.e: Fasting means going without food for a time. During Ramadan many adult Muslims do this every day.
63992.m: During Ramadan many Muslims fast during the day.

63993.q: From when until when do people fast each day during Ramadan?
a: From getting up until the morning snack
63993.e: The fast begins early in the morning when it gets light. It ends in the evening when the sun goes down.
63993.m: You fast from dawn until sunset.

63994.q: Are you allowed to drink water during the day when fasting in Ramadan?
a: Yes, as much as you like
Yes, but only in the morning
63994.e: When fasting in Ramadan, people go without food and any drink during the day. They only drink water again in the evening.
63994.m: When fasting in Ramadan you drink nothing during the day, not even water.

63995.q: Who does not have to fast during Ramadan?
63995.e: People who are ill need strength to get well. They are excused from fasting and can make up the days later.
63995.m: People who are ill do not have to fast during Ramadan.

63996.q: Roughly how long does Ramadan last?
63996.e: Ramadan is a whole month in the Islamic calendar. It has 29 or 30 days.

63997.q: Besides eating and drinking, what else should fasting Muslims avoid during Ramadan?
63997.e: Ramadan is not only about food. You should also be kind and not start arguments.
63997.m: During Ramadan you should also avoid arguing and unkind words.

63998.q: What is the meal eaten before dawn during Ramadan called?
63998.e: Before the fast, many families get up very early. They eat something before it gets light. This meal is called suhur.
63998.m: The meal early in the morning before the fast is called suhur.

63999.q: What is fasting in Ramadan for Muslims?
a: One of the five pillars of Islam
63999.e: Islam has five important duties, which are called pillars. Fasting in Ramadan is one of them.
63999.m: Fasting in Ramadan is one of the five pillars of Islam.

64000.q: Where do many Muslims like to pray together in the evening during Ramadan?
64000.e: During Ramadan many Muslims go to the mosque in the evening. There they say a special, long prayer called tarawih.
64000.m: During Ramadan many Muslims pray together at the mosque in the evening.

64001.q: Apart from fasting, what do many Muslims do especially often during Ramadan?
64001.e: Ramadan is a time for reflection. Many Muslims read the Quran more and go to the mosque more often to pray in the evening.
64001.m: During Ramadan many Muslims pray more and read the Quran.

64002.q: What does the word iftar mean?
64002.e: Iftar is an Arabic word. It means the evening meal with which you end the fast.

64003.q: When does iftar begin during Ramadan?
64003.e: As soon as the sun has set, the fast is over for that day. Then iftar begins.

64004.q: How was iftar announced in Cairo in the past?
64004.e: In Cairo a cannon used to be fired at sunset. That way everyone in the city knew they could eat again.
64004.m: In Cairo a cannon shot used to mark the end of the fast.

64005.q: Who do many Muslims eat iftar with?
64005.e: Iftar is a happy meal. Many families sit together and invite friends too.
64005.m: Many Muslims eat iftar with family and friends.

64006.q: Where is there often a shared iftar for lots of people during Ramadan?
64006.e: During Ramadan many mosques cook for lots of people. There everyone can break the fast together.
64006.m: Many mosques hold a shared iftar.

64007.q: What do many Muslims often drink first at iftar?
64007.e: After a long day without drinking you are thirsty. So many people first drink a sip of water before they eat properly.
64007.m: At iftar people often drink water first.

64008.q: Which soup do people in Morocco like to eat at iftar?
64008.e: Harira is a hearty soup from Morocco. It often contains tomatoes, lentils and chickpeas and is very popular at iftar.
64008.m: In Morocco people like to eat harira soup at iftar.

64009.q: Which bread is eaten in Turkey especially at iftar during Ramadan?
64009.e: In Turkey, bakeries bake a round, flat bread during Ramadan. It is called Ramadan pide and is eaten warm at iftar.
64009.m: In Turkey people like to eat Ramadan pide at iftar.

64010.q: Why do many Muslims also invite guests to iftar?
a: Because you may not eat alone
64010.e: During Ramadan people think especially of others. According to Islamic belief, giving others food is a very good deed.
64010.m: During Ramadan many Muslims like to share their food with guests.

64011.q: What is an open iftar, which some mosques in Switzerland invite people to?
a: Breaking the fast with all guests welcome
64011.e: At an open iftar everyone is welcome, including neighbours of a different religion. It is a way to get to know each other better.
64011.m: At an open iftar all guests are welcome.

64012.q: What do many Muslims first break their fast with in the evening?
64012.e: It is an old custom to end the fast with a sweet date. Many families put a bowl of dates on the table for this.
64012.m: Many Muslims break the fast with a date.

64013.q: What do the leaves of a date palm look like?
64013.e: At the top of its trunk the date palm has a crown of long leaves. These fronds are divided like feathers into many narrow parts.
64013.m: The date palm has long feathery fronds.

64014.q: On which tree do dates grow?
64014.e: Dates grow in large bunches high up on the date palm. One palm can carry a great many fruits.
64014.m: Dates grow on the date palm.

64015.q: Why are dates good after a long day of fasting?
a: They make you tired straight away
They contain a lot of fat
64015.e: The sugar from the date gets into the blood quickly. So after the fast the body soon has energy again.
64015.m: Dates quickly give new energy after fasting.

64016.q: In what kind of places do date palms grow well?
64016.e: Date palms love sun and heat. But they need water at their roots, for example from groundwater.
64016.m: Date palms grow in hot, dry places.

64017.q: What do you call a green place with water in the desert, where date palms often grow?
64017.e: In an oasis there is water in the middle of the desert. Plants such as the date palm can grow there.
64017.m: An oasis is a green place with water in the desert.

64018.q: What colour are dried dates usually?
64018.e: Fresh dates are yellow or red depending on the variety. When dried they usually turn brown and wrinkly.

64019.e: Every date has a hard, long stone inside. You only eat the sweet flesh around it.
64019.m: A date has a long stone inside.

64020.q: Which country is one of the world's biggest date growers (as of 2024)?
64020.e: Saudi Arabia and Egypt each harvest almost two million tonnes of dates a year (as of 2024). Algeria and Iran also harvest a great many.
64020.m: Saudi Arabia harvests a great many dates.

64021.q: What do many Muslims look for in the sky to know when the festival of breaking the fast begins?
64021.e: The Islamic calendar follows the moon. When the new, thin crescent moon is seen after Ramadan, the festival begins.
64021.m: The new crescent moon marks the start of the festival.

64022.q: What does the Arabic word “Eid” mean in English?
64022.e: Eid is the Arabic word for festival. That is why the names of the two great Islamic festivals begin with Eid.
64022.m: The Arabic word Eid means festival.

64023.q: What other name is the festival of breaking the fast often given in Switzerland?
64023.e: The name comes from the Turkish words Şeker Bayramı. So many families in Switzerland call it the Sugar Festival.
64023.m: The festival of breaking the fast is also called the Sugar Festival.

64024.q: What do Muslims wish each other at the festival of breaking the fast?
64024.e: “Eid Mubarak” is Arabic and means “blessed festival”. People say it as a greeting on the festival day.
64024.m: At the festival people wish each other “Eid Mubarak”.

64025.q: What do many Muslims do on the morning of the festival of breaking the fast?
a: They go to the festival prayer
64025.e: The festival day begins with a special prayer in the morning. Many people go to the mosque in festive clothes for it.
64025.m: The festival begins in the morning with the festival prayer.

64026.q: What do many children like to wear at the festival of breaking the fast?
64026.e: People dress up for the festival day. Many children get something new to wear for it.
64026.m: On the festival day many children wear nice new clothes.

64027.q: When does the festival of breaking the fast begin?
a: On the first day after Ramadan
On the first day of Ramadan
64027.e: The festival is celebrated straight after the month of fasting. It is the first day of the next month in the Islamic calendar.
64027.m: The festival of breaking the fast begins on the day after Ramadan.

64028.q: For how many days do many Muslims celebrate the festival of breaking the fast?
64028.e: In many countries the festival lasts three days. In Turkey, for example, these days are public holidays.
64028.m: The festival of breaking the fast usually lasts three days.

64029.q: In many countries, where does the festival prayer take place because so many people come?
64029.e: So many people come to the festival prayer that the mosques are often too small. That is why in many countries people pray in the open air.
64029.m: The festival prayer often takes place in a large open-air square.

64030.q: In which month was the festival of breaking the fast in 2026?
64030.e: In 2026 the month of fasting lasted from mid-February to mid-March. The festival fell on 20 March 2026.
64030.m: In 2026 the festival of breaking the fast was in March.

64031.q: Which is the most important festival in Islam?
64031.e: The Festival of Sacrifice is seen as the most important festival in Islam. It is celebrated at the time of the great pilgrimage.
64031.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is the most important festival in Islam.

64032.q: What is the Festival of Sacrifice called in Arabic?
64032.e: The word adha has to do with sacrifice. Eid al-Adha is the Arabic name for the Festival of Sacrifice.
64032.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is called Eid al-Adha in Arabic.

64033.q: According to Islamic tradition, what was the name of the son Ibrahim was to sacrifice?
64033.e: Most Muslim scholars say it was Ismail. In the Bible the son in this story is called Isaac.
64033.m: According to Islamic tradition, Ibrahim was to sacrifice his son Ismail.

64034.q: Which animals are often sacrificed at the Festival of Sacrifice?
64034.e: For the Festival of Sacrifice a healthy animal is slaughtered, usually a sheep, a goat or a cow. In some countries it is also a camel.
64034.m: At the Festival of Sacrifice people often sacrifice a sheep, goat or cow.

64035.q: In Switzerland, what must always happen to mammals such as sheep before slaughter?
64035.e: In Switzerland it is forbidden to slaughter mammals without stunning them. This also applies to animals sacrificed for the Festival of Sacrifice.
64035.m: In Switzerland mammals must be stunned before slaughter.

64036.q: What are many Muslims doing in Mecca at the time of the Festival of Sacrifice?
64036.e: Every year millions of Muslims travel to Mecca. The Festival of Sacrifice falls during the days of this great pilgrimage, the Hajj.
64036.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is celebrated at the time of the pilgrimage to Mecca.

64037.q: What is the Festival of Sacrifice called in Turkish?
64037.e: Kurban means sacrifice and bayram means festival. Many Turkish families in Switzerland call the festival this.
64037.m: In Turkish the Festival of Sacrifice is called Kurban Bayramı.

64038.q: How long does the Festival of Sacrifice usually last?
64038.e: The Festival of Sacrifice begins on the tenth day of the pilgrimage month. It usually lasts four days.
64038.m: The Festival of Sacrifice usually lasts four days.

64039.q: When was the Festival of Sacrifice in 2026?
64039.e: In 2026 the Festival of Sacrifice began around 27 May. Because the festival follows the moon, it falls on a different date every year.
64039.m: In 2026 the Festival of Sacrifice was at the end of May.

64040.q: What does the story of Ibrahim at the Festival of Sacrifice stand for?
64040.e: Ibrahim trusted God completely. That is why Muslims see him as a model of faith.
64040.m: The story of Ibrahim shows great trust in God.

64041.q: What must be seen in the sky for a new Islamic month to begin?
64041.e: A new month begins when the first thin crescent moon can be seen after the new moon. That is why many people watch the sky carefully in the evening.
64041.m: An Islamic month begins with the new crescent moon.

64042.q: What is the new, thin crescent moon called in Arabic?
64042.e: The Arabic word hilal means crescent moon. When the hilal is seen, a new month begins.
64042.m: The crescent moon is called hilal in Arabic.

64043.q: What do you see in the sky at new moon?
64043.e: At new moon the moon is between the Earth and the sun. Its bright side faces away from us, so we can hardly see it.
64043.m: At new moon you can hardly see the moon.

64044.q: Roughly how long is it from one new moon to the next?
64044.e: The moon takes about 29 and a half days to look the same again. That is why a lunar month has 29 or 30 days.
64044.m: From new moon to new moon is about 29 and a half days.

64045.q: Which flag shows a white crescent moon and a star on a red background?
64045.e: The Turkish flag is red with a white crescent moon and a white star. Other countries also have a crescent moon on their flag.
64045.m: The Turkish flag shows a crescent moon and a star.

64046.q: What is the counterpart of the Red Cross called in many Muslim countries?
64046.e: The Red Cross was founded in Geneva. In many Muslim countries the same movement helps people under the sign of a red crescent.
64046.m: The Red Crescent helps people just like the Red Cross.

64047.q: Where can you see a crescent moon on many mosques?
a: Right at the top of the dome or minaret
64047.e: Many mosques have a golden crescent moon on top of the dome or minaret. It is a well-known symbol of Islam.
64047.m: Many mosques have a crescent moon on top.

64048.q: At what time of day do people look out for the new crescent moon?
64048.e: The new crescent moon is very thin and sets soon after the sun. You can only see it briefly at dusk.
64048.m: You look for the new crescent moon in the evening after sunset.

64049.q: In which direction do you see the new crescent moon in the evening?
64049.e: The new crescent moon is close to the sun in the sky. In the evening the sun sets in the west, and that is where you see the crescent too.
64049.m: In the evening you see the new crescent moon in the west.

64050.q: What happens if clouds hide the new crescent moon?
a: People wait for the full moon
64050.e: An Islamic month has at most 30 days. If the crescent cannot be seen, people simply count to 30 and then start the new month.
64050.m: If the crescent moon cannot be seen, the month has 30 days.

64051.q: What does the Islamic calendar follow?
64051.e: Every month in the Islamic calendar begins with a new moon. That is why it is called a lunar calendar.
64051.m: The Islamic calendar follows the moon.

64052.q: How many months does an Islamic year have?
64052.e: Like our calendar, the Islamic calendar has twelve months. But the months are shorter.
64052.m: An Islamic year has twelve months.

64053.q: How long is an Islamic year compared with our year?
64053.e: Twelve lunar months together are shorter than a solar year. An Islamic year has only about 354 days.
64053.m: An Islamic year is about 11 days shorter than our year.

64054.q: Is Ramadan in the same month of our calendar every year?
a: No, it moves through the year
64054.e: The Islamic calendar follows the moon and is shorter than our year. So Ramadan begins a little earlier in our calendar every year. That way it sometimes falls in summer and sometimes in winter.

64055.q: Which month of the Islamic calendar is Ramadan?
64055.e: Ramadan is the ninth of twelve months. It is the best-known month of the Islamic year.
64055.m: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.

64056.q: What do Muslims celebrate on the first day of the Islamic year?
64056.e: The Islamic year begins with the month of Muharram. The first day is the Islamic New Year.
64056.m: The first day of the Islamic year is New Year.

64057.q: Why is the Islamic year number much smaller than ours?
a: Because every other year is left out
64057.e: The Islamic count of years only begins in the 7th century AD. That is why the number is smaller: in summer 2026, for example, the year 1448 began.
64057.m: The Islamic count of years started later than ours.

64058.q: When does a new day begin in the Islamic calendar?
64058.e: In the Islamic calendar the day begins in the evening. That is why some festivals are already celebrated the evening before.
64058.m: In the Islamic calendar the day begins at sunset.

64059.q: Which month is the month of the pilgrimage to Mecca?
64059.e: The great pilgrimage takes place in the last month of the Islamic year. It is called Dhu al-Hijjah.
64059.m: The pilgrimage is in the twelfth month of the Islamic year.

64060.q: Roughly how long does it take for Ramadan to move through all the seasons?
64060.e: Every year Ramadan moves by about eleven days. After roughly 33 years it is back in the same season.
64060.m: Ramadan moves through all the seasons in about 33 years.

64061.q: What is the colourful lantern that many children carry during Ramadan called?
64061.e: The fanous is a beautiful lantern with coloured windows. For many children it is part of Ramadan.
64061.m: The Ramadan lantern is called a fanous.

64062.q: In which country are Ramadan lanterns especially well known?
64062.e: In Egypt lanterns hang in the streets everywhere during Ramadan. Today they are popular in other Arab countries too.
64062.m: Ramadan lanterns are especially well known in Egypt.

64063.q: In which city is the tradition of Ramadan lanterns said to have begun?
64063.e: An old story tells that over 1,000 years ago the people of Cairo welcomed a ruler with lanterns. The custom is said to have grown from that.
64063.m: The custom of Ramadan lanterns is said to have begun in Cairo.

64064.q: What are traditional Ramadan lanterns made of?
64064.e: Craftspeople shape a frame from tin or copper. In between they set coloured panes of glass, through which the light shimmers.
64064.m: Traditional Ramadan lanterns are made of metal and coloured glass.

64065.q: What do children in Egypt often do with their lanterns during Ramadan?
a: They sing songs with them in the street
They throw them into the Nile
They bury them in the sand
64065.e: In the evening children walk through the lanes with their glowing lanterns. As they go, they sing cheerful Ramadan songs.
64065.m: Children sing Ramadan songs with their lanterns.

64066.q: What do the many lanterns and lights during Ramadan show?
a: The end of the school year
64066.e: The lights decorate houses and streets. They show that people are happy about the special month.
64066.m: The Ramadan lights show joy about the holy month.

64067.q: Where do Ramadan lanterns often hang in Egypt?
a: Across the lanes and on houses
64067.e: During Ramadan people stretch strings across the lanes. Lanterns and lights hang from them and glow in the evening.
64067.m: In Egypt the lanterns hang across the lanes.

64068.q: What were lanterns used for at night in the past?
64068.e: In the past there were no street lamps. With a lantern you could find your way to the mosque or home at night.
64068.m: In the past lanterns helped people find their way in the dark.

64069.q: What can some modern plastic Ramadan lanterns do?
64069.e: Today there are also plastic lanterns with batteries. They light up in colours, and some play Ramadan songs.
64069.m: Some modern Ramadan lanterns light up and play music.

64070.q: What shapes do many Ramadan lights on houses and windows have?
64070.e: Many families decorate their homes with lights during Ramadan. Crescent moons and stars are especially popular.
64070.m: Ramadan lights are often shaped like a crescent moon and star.
